digest.component_or_area: tracker initialization and op-cert attestation system
propositions: Cloning or rebuilding the tracker without preserving .env-id causes a new environment identity to be minted, silently invalidating all op-cert attestations signed by the prior environment
The .env-id ensure-registry unit and _gen_local_files mint a fresh UUID whenever .env-id is absent, with no check for whether the store already contains events written by a different environment
Re-identifying the environment is never caught at re-clone time; the failure surfaces hours later as a foreign_key verdict on an unrelated gate operation

Minting .env-id over a store that already holds events from another environment must emit a loud stderr warning naming the prior env id(s), the attestation consequence, the git-ignored carry-over list, and the override switch REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1

rebar fsck must detect and report ENV_ID_MISMATCH as a counted issue when the current environment's own author(s) also wrote events under a different env_id, indicating a re-identification or same-person environment change
